findings.claim: The switch in the unsigned-integer writer drops the `<= byte.MaxValue` case, so values 128..255 now fall through to TryWriteUInt16 and are encoded as uint16 (0xcd) instead of the canonical uint8 (0xcc). Output is non-canonical and larger. Readers still decode it, so this is not a security hole. The change is unrelated to the requirement and alters the wire format, so it breaks byte-compat for hash- or signature-based consumers, and any strict-format expectations.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize uint values 128, 200 and 255 (and an int in that range) with base-built and head-built MessagePack. Compare bytes: base emits CC xx, head emits CD 00 xx. Also run the existing MessagePackWriter/Primitives tests.

findings.claim: ReportIfLocatedInCompilation drops every diagnostic whose location is not in the compilation. It also drops diagnostics with a null Location, which Diagnostic.Create turns into Location.None. Diagnostics that guard users against insecure or unsupported configurations can then be silently lost whenever a location lookup returns null, for example GetPropertyIdentifierLocation returning null for a non-PropertyDeclarationSyntax such as a record positional parameter. The result is a silent failure to warn, not a crash. The diagnostics affected are mostly compile-time diagnostics such as MsgPack004 and MsgPack00x, so the security impact is low.

receipt_plan.detail: Add an analyzer test with a [MessagePackObject] record whose positional property lacks a Key and has a null location. Assert that the expected MsgPack diagnostic is still reported, before and after the change.
